judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's four cited results are all correct. S4 = 1 - 1/8 + 1/27 - 1/64 = (1728 - 216 + 64 - 27)/1728 = 1549/1728, with the alternating-series bound |a5| = 1/125 (id 4); the telescoping sum of 1/(n(n+3)) is (1/3)(1 + 1/2 + 1/3) = 11/18 (id 6); 1/(N+1)^2 < 1/100 needs N + 1 > 10, so N = 10 with bound 1/121 (id 8); and the ratio test on n(x-2)^n/5^n gives |x-2|/5, so R = 5 about x = 2 (id 9). The improper integrals check out too: the integral of 1/x^2 from 1 to infinity is 1 (id 3) and of 1/(x ln^2 x) from 2 to infinity is 1/ln 2 (id 7). The three manual entries (1(b), 6(a), 10) correctly separate the comparison ARGUMENTS from the machine-checkable sums. But 32/32 is not defensible once you read the delivered Quick Answers bank against the stems. Problem 9 asks for the radius of convergence and 'the open interval on which the ratio test guarantees convergence'. The only verify entry under id 9 is a limit of ((n+1)/5^(n+1))/(n/5^n) with expected 1/5 - the coefficient ratio, an intermediate quantity - and the bank prints '9. 1/5'. Neither requested answer is there: the key's own boxed line reads 'L = (1/5)|x-2|, R = 5, (-3, 7)'. A grader marking from the bank would mark a student who correctly writes R = 5 and (-3,7) as wrong. Problem 8 has the same shape: it asks for the smallest N AND the bound, verify.json binds only 1/(n+1)^2 at n = 10 - feeding the answer in as an input - and the bank prints '8. 1/121', so N = 10 appears nowhere in the verified data. Third, and independently confirmable with pdfinfo: final_response.md states 'Answer key (ak_series_curr497.pdf, 5 pages)' and the built answer_key.pdf has 4 pages. Fourth, minor, the bank prints '7. 1/log(2)' where the worksheet and key write ln.

strengths_to_preserve: The three manual entries are placed with real discrimination. Ids 1 and 6 each carry a machine entry for the sum (3/2 and 11/18) plus a manual entry whose desc states the exact comparison chain the student must produce - '0 < 1/(3^n + n) <= 1/3^n for every n >= 0, and the larger series converges' - so the checkable half and the argued half of a comparison-test item live under one id without either being mistaken for the other.

Problem 7 is the sheet's best-engineered item: the integral test on 1/(n ln^2 n) requires the u = ln x substitution, gives the exact value 1/ln 2, and the worksheet says the substitution 'helps' rather than performing it. The exact answer is a logarithm rather than a decimal, which is what the directions box demands throughout.

Problem 6 pairs a direct comparison with a telescoping evaluation of the SAME series: part (a) proves convergence against the p = 2 series, part (b) uses the partial-fraction identity 1/(n(n+3)) = (1/3)(1/n - 1/(n+3)) to get 11/18 exactly. Proving convergence and then producing the value are separate skills, and the item makes the student do both on one object.

root_causes.description: On problems 8 and 9 the verified quantity is an intermediate step rather than the answer the stem requests. Id 9 binds the coefficient ratio 1/5 instead of the radius R = 5 or the interval (-3,7); id 8 binds the bound 1/121 while feeding the requested N = 10 in as an input. Because the quick-answer bank is generated from the expected values, the delivered bank prints answers to questions the worksheet did not ask.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 9: 'find the radius of convergence ... then state the open interval on which the ratio test guarantees convergence' - verify.json id 9 is one limit entry with expected 1/5
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '9. 1/5'; answer_key.pdf boxed line for problem 9: 'L = (1/5)|x - 2|, R = 5, (-3, 7)'

worksheet.pdf problem 8: 'find the smallest number of terms N ... and give the bound |a_{N+1}| as an exact fraction' - verify.json id 8 is {"type":"eval","expr":"1/(n+1)**2","at":{"n":10},"expected":"1/121"}, so N = 10 is an input, and the bank prints '8. 1/121'

root_causes.description: The final response's page count for the answer key was narrated rather than measured: it claims 5 pages against a built PDF of 4.

improvements.title: Problem 9 banks the ratio-test intermediate 1/5 instead of R = 5 and (-3, 7); problem 8 omits N = 10
improvements.proposed_change: Require that every quantity a stem names as an answer has its own verify entry, and that no id's ONLY entry is an intermediate. Concretely: id 9 needs a solve or eval binding R = 5 and an entry binding the interval endpoints -3 and 7 in addition to the coefficient limit; id 8 needs an entry that SOLVES 1/(N+1)^2 < 1/100 for the smallest integer N rather than evaluating at a supplied N = 10. Add a gate rule that flags an id whose entries are all of type limit when the stem's answer nouns ('radius', 'interval', 'smallest N') are absent from every entry's note or expected.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a stem reading 'find the radius of convergence ... then state the open interval' with a single limit entry expected 1/5. The gate must fail naming the unbound answers. Adding entries for R = 5 and the interval passes, and the regenerated bank must contain '5' and '(-3, 7)'. The fixture passes today and the bank prints only 1/5.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader marking from the bank stops seeing an intermediate where the requested answer should be, which is the difference between marking a correct power-series answer right and marking it wrong.
improvements.risk: Medium. Matching answer nouns against entries is heuristic; it should warn loudly and require an explicit author acknowledgement rather than hard-failing on ambiguous stems.

improvements.title: final_response.md says the answer key is 5 pages; pdfinfo reports 4
improvements.proposed_change: Generate the page counts instead of writing them. Have build.sh run pdfinfo on each built PDF and emit the three counts into a small generated fragment that the final response includes, or add a delivery check that parses '(<file>, N pages)' patterns out of final_response.md and compares each N against pdfinfo, failing the build on any mismatch.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a final_response.md claiming '5 pages' beside a 4-page answer_key.pdf. The delivery check must exit non-zero reporting 'answer_key.pdf: claimed 5, actual 4'. Correcting the number passes. No such check exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: Ends the narrated-page-count class of defect (curr-113, curr-126, curr-144 and this case) at essentially zero cost.
improvements.risk: Low. The only care needed is a tolerant parser for the several phrasings the responses use.

case_summary: Rigorous convergence-test fluency practice with a genuine ramp across the direct comparison, integral, ratio and alternating-series tests, and three manual entries that correctly carve comparison arguments out from machine-checkable sums. I re-derived every verified quantity - S4 = 1549/1728 with bound 1/125, the telescoping 11/18, the improper integrals 1 and 1/ln 2, the ratio limits, and N = 10 with bound 1/121 - and found no mathematical error, so the judge's content assessment stands. The perfect 32/32 does not, because of what the delivered answer key prints. Problem 9 asks for the radius and the open interval; the only verify entry is the coefficient ratio 1/5 and the Quick Answers bank prints '9. 1/5', while the key's own boxed line gives R = 5 and (-3,7). Problem 8 asks for the smallest N and the bound; N = 10 is fed in as a verify input rather than solved for, so the bank prints only '8. 1/121'. A grader working from the bank would mark a correct student wrong on problem 9. Separately, final_response.md claims the answer key is 5 pages and pdfinfo reports 4, and the bank prints 1/log(2) where the document writes 1/ln 2.
